preconditions.description: Every line after the first in stdin is a non-empty string of digits representing a test case number N.
The first line of stdin is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(line) <= 18 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each test case number N has between 1 and 18 digits (inclusive).

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the integer T (number of test cases), matching the input.
The total number of lines in stdout is exactly T + 1 (one line per test case answer plus the T line).
Each line after the first in stdout is a non-empty string of digits representing the rank of the corresponding test case number N.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line) <= factorial(len(N)) for N, line in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: For each test case N, the rank is a positive integer between 1 and the factorial of the number of digits in N (inclusive), representing the 1-based position of N in the lexicographically sorted list of all permutations of its digits.

postconditions.expression: all(rank == compute_rank(N) for N, rank in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: For each test case N, the rank is computed as the 1-based index of N in the sorted list of all unique permutations of its digits, where permutations are ordered lexicographically. The function compute_rank(N) is defined as follows: (1) Generate all unique permutations of the digits of N, (2) sort them lexicographically, (3) return the 1-based index of N in this sorted list.
